**The Girl Who Wanted to Be Full**

In a small, forgotten town where the streets were cracked and the air smelled of damp earth, there lived a girl named Lina. She was thin—painfully so—with sharp collarbones that jutted out like the ribs of a starving bird. Her family was poor, so poor that sometimes the only thing she ate in a day was a single slice of stale bread, dipped in water to soften it. She hated her body. She hated how her clothes hung off her like rags on a scarecrow, how her wrists looked like twigs, how her stomach never stopped growling.

*"If only I were fat,"* she would whisper to herself at night, pressing her hands against her flat belly. *"If only I could be full."*

One day, she heard about a job at *The Golden Spoon*, a rundown restaurant on the edge of town. The food was greasy, the portions were small, and the customers rarely finished their meals—leaving behind mountains of leftovers. Lina saw her chance.

She marched into the restaurant, her bare feet slapping against the sticky floor, and found the owner, a tired man with a permanent scowl. *"I’ll work for free,"* she said, her voice trembling but determined. *"No wages. Just a place to sleep and whatever food is left at the end of the night."*

The owner blinked. *"You want to work for scraps?"*

*"Yes,"* Lina said, her eyes burning. *"And I’ll eat every bite."*

The owner shrugged. *"Fine. But if you steal, I’ll throw you out."*

Lina didn’t steal. She *ate*.

At first, it was just the leftovers—cold fries, half-eaten burgers, the greasy remains of stews. But soon, she started sneaking extra portions when the cooks weren’t looking. Then she began eating the food meant for the trash—overcooked meat, burnt bread, anything that could fill her. The owner noticed, but he didn’t stop her. After all, she was still working for free.

Weeks passed. Then months.

Lina’s ribs disappeared beneath layers of soft flesh. Her arms grew thick, her stomach rounded, her thighs pressed together when she walked. She waddled now, her breath coming in short gasps. The other waitresses whispered behind her back, but Lina didn’t care. She was *full*. For the first time in her life, she was *full*.

Then, one day, she tried to leave the restaurant.

The door wouldn’t open.

She pressed her hands against the wood, but her belly was too wide, her hips too broad. She turned sideways, sucking in her breath, but it was no use. She was trapped.

The owner sighed. *"You’re too big."*

Lina panicked. She tried the bathroom door next, but it was even narrower. She couldn’t fit. She couldn’t *move*.

The owner shook his head. *"You’ll have to stay in the kitchen. I’ll bring you food."*

And so she did.

At first, it wasn’t so bad. She slept on a pile of old tablecloths, ate whatever was left, and never had to worry about hunger again. But as the months passed, her body grew heavier, softer, *larger*. She couldn’t stand for long, so she sat on the floor, her back against the wall, her legs spread wide to support her weight. The kitchen became her world.

Then the smell started.

At first, it was just a faint sourness in the air. But as Lina’s hygiene worsened—she couldn’t reach to wash herself, couldn’t fit through the door to the bathroom—the stench grew. It seeped into the dining area, thick and cloying, like rotting meat and sweat. Customers wrinkled their noses. Some left without ordering. Others complained.

The owner tried to ignore it. *"Just a bad drain,"* he lied.

But the smell only got worse.

Soon, the restaurant was empty. No one came. The owner’s savings dwindled. Bills piled up. One by one, the staff quit, unable to stand the stench. Finally, the owner locked the doors for the last time, leaving a note on the window: *"Closed for good."*

Lina didn’t notice at first. She was too busy eating.

But when the deliveries stopped, when the last of the canned food ran out, she realized—she was alone.

The restaurant was silent. Dust settled on the tables. The kitchen was dark, the only light coming from the cracks in the boarded-up windows. Lina sat in the corner, her body too large to move, her skin slick with sweat and grime. She had no way out. No way to clean herself. No way to escape the prison she had made of her own body.

And yet, when she closed her eyes, she smiled.

Because she was *full*.

And for the first time in her life, she was exactly what she had always wanted to be.
